title_en: Ferdinand Lassalle, Die Philosophie Herakleitos des Dunklen von Ephesos, new edition (E. Schirmer, about 1905): front cover
title_el: Ferdinand Lassalle, Die Philosophie Herakleitos des Dunklen von Ephesos, νέα έκδοση (E. Schirmer, περ. 1905): εξώφυλλο
licence: Not in copyright (Internet Archive item record: possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT)
attribution: Public domain. Scan: Robarts Library, University of Toronto, via the Internet Archive
note: On the cover (src/assets/nostos-covers/vintage/): the library barcode is left, because it covers the first letter of the title. Grey cover printed in black and red, with the title in Fraktur. Volume 1 of the 'Neue Ausgabe' edited by E. Schirmer; the title page is undated and 1905 comes from the Internet Archive record. Lassalle's study (first published 1858) is built on 'a new collection of his fragments and the testimonies of the ancients' (subtitle), so it is a German study, not a plain edition or translation. A barcode at the top left. A plainer English option that also qualifies: Burnet, Early Greek Philosophy, 2nd ed. (A. and C. Black, 1908), University of California copy (archive.org/details/burnetgreek00burnrich), plain black cloth.

title_en: Plutarch, Essays and Miscellanies, vol. 4, ed. Goodwin (Little, Brown, 1911): front cover
title_el: Πλούταρχος, Δοκίμια και ποικίλα (Ηθικά), τόμ. 4, επιμ. Goodwin (Little, Brown, 1911): εξώφυλλο
licence: Not in copyright (Internet Archive item record: possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT)
attribution: Public domain. Scan: Boston Public Library, via the Internet Archive
note: Plain maroon cloth with nothing on the front: a last resort. The volume contains 'Of the Word EI Engraven over the Gate of Apollo's Temple at Delphi' (the E at Delphi), in the 'several hands' translation revised by W. W. Goodwin. Copyright 1870, 1898, 1905; the Internet Archive record dates this printing 1911. From the personal library of James Buell Munn. Also qualifying: Prickard, Selected Essays of Plutarch, vol. II (Clarendon Press, 1918), which has 'The E at Delphi', Toronto copy (archive.org/details/selectedessaysof02plutuoft), bright green cloth with a barcode. King's Theosophical Essays (Bohn) did not turn up in an Internet Archive title search.

title_en: Plato, Opera, vol. 4 (Timaeus), ed. Burnet, Oxford Classical Texts (Clarendon Press, first published 1902): front cover
title_el: Πλάτων, Άπαντα, τόμ. 4 (Τίμαιος), επιμ. Burnet, Oxford Classical Texts (Clarendon Press, πρώτη έκδοση 1902): εξώφυλλο
licence: Not in copyright (Internet Archive item record: possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT). Does NOT meet the 1900 to 1930 rule for certain: this copy was printed by John Johnson, Printer to the University from 1925 to 1946, so it may be a printing after 1930.
attribution: Scan: Robarts Library, University of Toronto, via the Internet Archive
note: On the cover (src/assets/nostos-covers/vintage/): a library barcode at the top left painted out with the cloth below it. NEAREST OPTION, NOT A QUALIFYING ONE. Plain red cloth with a barcode at the top left; nothing printed on the front. Volume 4 holds Clitophon, Republic, Timaeus and Critias. Imprint: 'Londini et Novi Eboraci apud Humphredum Milford', 'Excudebat Ioannes Johnson'. No 1900 to 1930 cover of the Timaeus with a stated licence was found: the Loeb Timaeus (Bury, 1929) exists only as Internet Archive copies whose records give no rights statement (for example bwb_S0-EHE-311, plain dark cloth), and the scans that show a Loeb dust jacket are modern reprints.

title_en: Plato, Cratylus and Theaetetus (Greek), ed. Hermann and Wohlrab, Bibliotheca Teubneriana (Teubner, 1902): front cover

licence: Not stated: the Internet Archive record (PIMS library, University of Toronto) has no rights or copyright-status field. Book published in Leipzig in 1902.
attribution: Scan: Pontifical Institute of Mediaeval Studies library, University of Toronto, via the Internet Archive
note: On the cover (src/assets/nostos-covers/vintage/): the library label at the lower left painted out with the mirror image of the frame on the right. NEAREST OPTION, NOT A QUALIFYING ONE, because the record states no licence. Orange printed cloth in the same Teubner Art Nouveau frame as the Phaedrus and the Ethics: 'Plato 2: Cratylus Theaetetus, ediderunt C. Fr. Hermann, M. Wohlrab'. A call-number label (B 367 .A1 1902 IMS) at the lower left. The OCR of the opening pages includes a Teubner notice dated 1906, so this binding is from about 1906. The only Cratylus covers with a stated licence are later printings: Burnet's Oxford text, vol. 1 (Toronto, archive.org/details/platonisopera01platuoft), printed by John Johnson (1925 to 1946), plain black with a barcode.

Kern's Orphicorum fragmenta (Weidmann, 1922; Toronto, NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT) is a 20th-century Orphic edition but leaves the Hymns out, and its copy is in a plain library binding.

note: On the cover (src/assets/nostos-covers/vintage/): the white margins of the scan cropped off.
